A ten-week plan

The roadmap

About an hour a day. Each week ends with that book's quiz; the last week is pure revision with the interview banks.

  1. Weeks 1–2Java Core

    The JVM, OOP in Java, collections internals, streams, then concurrency: threads, locks, executors and CompletableFuture.

    Open Java Core →
  2. Weeks 3–4Spring Boot

    IoC and beans, the request flow, JPA and transactions, security with JWT, testing, then Spring Boot 4 and microservices.

    Open Spring Boot →
  3. Weeks 5–7System Design

    HLD building blocks, the case studies (Netflix, UPI, Stripe, JioHotstar), SOLID, design patterns and the LLD projects.

    Open System Design →
  4. Week 8Cloud & DevOps

    AWS and GCP core services, Docker, Kubernetes, CI/CD, deploying a Spring Boot app, and the Linux commands you'll use every day.

    Open Cloud & DevOps →
  5. Week 9AI Engineering

    How LLMs work, embeddings, RAG from basic to advanced, agents and tool calling, MCP, and building it all in Java with Spring AI.

    Open AI Engineering →
  6. Week 10Revision

    Each book's cheat sheet, the interview question banks ("I can answer this" ticks), and the quizzes in "retry my mistakes" mode.

    Back to the books →

One story, five books

Ramu's chai business teaches everything

Ramu starts with a tea stall in Medinipur. In each book his business grows a little, and every problem he hits is a real engineering problem in disguise.

Java Core

Ramu's kitchen: chefs are threads, the order board is shared memory, and two chefs grabbing the same pan is a deadlock.

Spring Boot

The franchise kit: head office hires and wires your staff (IoC), and the kit arrives pre-assembled (auto-configuration).

System Design

The national chain: more stalls (scaling), a manager at the gate (load balancer), flasks on the counter (cache).

Cloud & DevOps

Ramu rents kitchens in a food court instead of building his own, and ships a sealed tiffin box (container) to each one.

AI Engineering

Ramu hires an AI assistant that reads his recipe book before answering (RAG) and plugs into his tools through one standard socket (MCP).
